newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trade on Wednesday with technical charts showing a weak market trend, traders said.
With the approach of its final trading day on July 14, the July 1997 contract was the most actively traded at levels higher than other contracts.
It ended today's session at 3,312 yuan ($400) per tonne, down 43 yuan from Friday's close. The market was closed on Monday and Tuesday to celebrate the Chinese takeover of Hong Kong.
September rose 88 to 3,288, November fell 27 to 3,276, the January 1998 contract 119 to 3,215 and March 16 to 3,296.
Combined volume fell to 23,700 tonnes from 28,000.
Soybeans opened mostly down and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Investors are unwilling to build long positions above the 3,300-yuan level as technical charts show strong selling pressure at that level, which made most contracts fall today," one trader said.
"Most investors would rather stay on the sidelines due to a lack of fresh incentives," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to fall steadily in the next few days. ($1=8.2900 yuan)
